system.name: ThinkAct
system.one_liner: A dual-system vision-language-action framework: an MLLM reasons, trained with GRPO and an action-aligned visual reward, and conditions a downstream action model.

content.variant_note: feedback box and a thinking robot on the left fan out into three aligned rows of capability, reasoning text and result
content.argues: Reasoning reinforced by action-aligned visual feedback lets a robot think before acting and gain few-shot adaptation, long-horizon planning and self-correction.
content.subject: A feedback box with two scored rollouts, a Thinking robot, and three rows pairing real reasoning text with its result.

lessons.what_to_learn: Show thinking before acting as a left-to-right fan-out: a feedback box with scored rollouts and a labelled curved arrow into a cartoon thinker, then one row per capability pairing real reasoning text with highlighted spans and its result through a big outlined arrow.
lessons.suits: agent or embodied-AI papers that claim several emergent capabilities and can back each with a text excerpt and a small result.

evidence: ThinkAct adopts a dual-system architecture that connects structured reasoning with executable actions.
we incentivize MLLMs to perform long-horizon planning by advancing reinforcement learning with an action-aligned reward
ThinkAct enables capabilities of few-shot adaptation, long-horizon planning, and self-correction in embodied tasks.

summary: ThinkAct is a dual-system vision-language-action framework in which a multimodal LLM reasons before an action model acts, trained with GRPO and an action-aligned visual reward. Figure 1 reads left to right. A grey-framed Action-Aligned Visual Feedback box scores two rollouts of Put the strawberry in the drawer with goal-completion and trajectory-alignment ticks and crosses around a scale icon, and a curved arrow labelled GRPO leads to a cartoon robot with a lightbulb, Thinking. Three aligned rows then pair a capability label (Few-Shot Adaptation, Long-Horizon Planning, Self-Correction) with a dashed box of real reasoning text with highlighted spans, a big outlined arrow, and a result: a 10-shot LIBERO bar chart with a 25.1% gain, frame strips, and a dropped-object recovery.
summary_zh: ThinkAct 是先推理后行动的双系统视觉-语言-动作框架。图 1 自左向右：带对错标记的动作对齐视觉反馈框经 GRPO 箭头指向“思考”机器人，再分三行展示少样本适应、长程规划与自我纠正的推理文本、结果柱状图和机器人帧序列。
notes: Prior labels kept in order (stage-pipeline as fan-out, contribution-mosaic as capability rows, worked-walkthrough for the real reasoning text and frames). The fan-out from the Thinking robot to the three rows is implied by position; no line joins them. Panel count is 1 because the dashed boxes are untitled parts of three aligned rows. The digest counts no dashed shapes although the boxes are drawn dashed, so the dashes may be part of placed artwork. The origin of the cartoon robot and robot-arm picture (stock or generated) is unknown.
